original_question: Is any of the three Borel-cover classes S_1(B_Ω, B_Γ), S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) closed under taking finite powers of a space?
target_in_paper: Section 8.2, Problem 6: "Is any of the classes S_1(B_Ω, B_Γ), S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) closed under taking finite powers?" ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact trio of Borel selection classes and the exact preservation question from the paper: closure under finite powers. This matches Section 8.2, Problem 6 essentially verbatim. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's default ambient setting is that, unless otherwise indicated, the spaces under discussion are spaces homeomorphic to sets of reals; your draft phrases the problem for an arbitrary space. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

B_Ω and B_Γ should be made explicit: they are the families of countable Borel ω-covers and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively; likewise B denotes the family of countable Borel covers of X. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

S_1(U,V) and S_fin(U,V) should be defined in Scheepers' notation: from each sequence of covers in U one selects, respectively, one member or finitely many members from each cover so that the resulting family belongs to V. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

"Closed under taking finite powers" should be unpacked as: if X has the property, then X^n has the same property for every positive integer n. That quantifier is implicit in the paper's formulation. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

The nearby context notes that, in the Borel case, these are the only remaining candidates for finite-power preservation, and it gives a separate reformulation for the last two subcases in Problem 7. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is relevant here; this is a topological selection-principles question, not an algebraic one. This should simply be omitted rather than guessed. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
refined_question: For a set of reals X, let B_Ω(X) and B_Γ(X) denote the families of countable Borel ω-covers and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively, and let S_1(U,V) and S_fin(U,V) be the usual Scheepers selection principles. Which, if any, of the three Borel selection properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Γ), S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), and S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) are closed under taking finite powers; that is, if X satisfies one of these properties, must X^n satisfy the same property for every positive integer n? ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: For the last two subcases only, the paper explicitly reformulates the question as follows: if X satisfies S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), must every finite power X^n satisfy S_1(B, B)? And if X satisfies S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω), must every finite power X^n satisfy S_1(B_Γ, B)? Here B is the family of countable Borel covers of X. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 8.2, Problem 6 directly, not a broader neighboring question: it names exactly the same three Borel classes and asks exactly about preservation under finite powers. To make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import the earlier definitions of S_1 and S_fin from Section 2.1, the default scope of spaces from Section 2.3, and the meanings of B, B_Ω, and B_Γ from Section 3. I therefore sharpened the wording without broadening it, and I kept Problem 7 only as the paper's explicit reformulation of the last two subcases rather than replacing Problem 6 by that neighboring statement. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
